title: Mummies
objective: After this level you can explain how and why Egyptians mummified the dead.
summary: Egyptians believed the ka and ba needed a preserved body. Over about 70 days, embalmers removed organs, dried the body in natron and wrapped it in linen.

cards.headline: The first Egyptian mummies were made by the desert, not by people.
cards.body: Early bodies buried in shallow pits in the sand were dried out by its heat. Remember Level 3: the red land’s dry climate made it ideal for cemeteries. Later, Egyptians learned to do on purpose what the desert did by accident.

cards.headline: Why keep a body?
cards.body: Egyptians believed a person’s soul had several parts. The two most important, the ka and the ba, needed a well-preserved body they could recognize and return to. Without it, they could not survive. And there was a model to follow: in Level 33’s myth, Anubis embalmed and wrapped Osiris, making the first mummy. Every embalmer after that was copying a god.

events.label: The brain comes out through the nose, and is often thrown away
Lungs, stomach, liver and intestines go into canopic jars
Natron, a natural salt, dries the body
Layers of linen, with amulets tucked in

cards.headline: The heart stays home
cards.body: Through a cut in the side, embalmers removed the lungs, stomach, liver and intestines for the canopic jars. But the heart was usually left inside, because Egyptians saw it as the center of knowledge and emotions. The wrappings were linen, woven from flax like the flax farmers grew in Level 4. The whole job took about 70 days, and Herodotus, the Greek historian from Level 2, gave the same figure.

mascot.line: The heart stays in. Remember that: in the next level, it goes on the scales.

cards.headline: Mummies: explained
learned: The first mummies were dried by desert sand
The ka and ba needed a preserved body
Organs went into canopic jars; the heart stayed in
Natron dried the body; linen wrapped it; about 70 days in all

questions.prompt: About how long did the full Egyptian mummification process take?

options.label: About 40 days
options.rationale: That was the natron drying stage alone.

options.label: About 365 days
options.rationale: It took months, not a year.

questions.explanation: Mummification took about 70 days, the same figure Herodotus gave; about 40 of those were spent drying in natron.

questions.prompt: Why did embalmers usually leave the heart inside the body?

options.label: It was too hard to reach
options.rationale: Embalmers removed organs all around it.

options.label: Egyptians saw it as the center of knowledge and emotions
It dried out on its own in natron
options.rationale: The reason was belief, not chemistry.

options.label: It was kept in a canopic jar instead
options.rationale: The jars held lungs, stomach, liver and intestines.

questions.explanation: Egyptians saw the heart as the center of knowledge and emotions, so it stayed with the body.

questions.prompt: How did Egypt’s earliest mummies form without any embalmer?

options.label: The Nile flood soaked them in silt
options.rationale: Water would have done the opposite.

options.label: Hot, dry desert sand dried out the bodies buried in it
They were sealed inside pyramids
options.rationale: These were simple pits in the sand.

questions.explanation: Bodies buried in shallow pits in the desert were dried by its heat; the red land made ideal cemeteries.
